title: Cross-domain Multilingual Embedding Spotlight: Annotation Protocol & Clustering Sanity Snapshot
content:
Purpose:
This working doc describes a compact, low-friction annotation protocol and a small clustering sanity snapshot for onboarding new embedding models across domain shifts and multiple languages. The goal: rapid human-in-the-loop checks that catch the most common semantic search and clustering regressions when a model is introduced or updated. This is intentionally lightweight and meant for repeated runs (weekly or per-model-release).

Scope and motivation:
- Focus areas: semantic relevance (query -> doc ranking), clustering sanity (local neighborhood coherence), multilingual robustness (EN, ES, ZH, RU, AR), and a handful of brittle edge-cases (paraphrase, code-switch, named-entity disambiguation).
- Not a full-scale benchmark; complements larger embedsets by surfacing high-impact, actionable failures quickly.

Dataset composition (spotlight set):
- 250 total examples split into three micro-suites:
  1) Semantic search probes (120 pairs): short queries (1–12 tokens) paired with 3 candidate documents each (A: clearly relevant, B: related but partial, C: distractor).
  2) Clustering sanity buckets (100 items): 10 small clusters of 8–12 items each drawn from distinct domains (recipes, legal snippets, product descriptions, medical FAQ, travel tips) + 10 singleton noise items to check isolation.
  3) Multilingual parity checks (30 triplets): translation-equivalent pairs across EN/ES/ZH (10 triplets) plus language-specific paraphrase pairs (20).

Annotation protocol (for relevance tasks):
- Raters: 2 annotators per example for majority/consensus; adjudicator for ties.
- Relevance scale (integer):
  0 - Not relevant: no topical overlap.
  1 - Weakly relevant: shares an entity/topic but not helpful to user intent.
  2 - Relevant: answers or directly addresses the query.
  3 - Highly relevant: concise, complete answer; high precision.
- Instructions: emphasize user intent. For ambiguous queries, prefer the interpretation that results in higher usefulness unless clearly out-of-scope.
- Examples in the guide: (include 6 short exemplars with rationales)
  Q: "how to fix leaking faucet"
  Doc A (3): step-by-step replacement of washer + tools list — rationale: direct resolution.
  Doc B (2): explanation of types of faucets with brief note on leaks — rationale: useful but not procedural.
  Doc C (0): blog about home decor mentioning taps — rationale: topical but not relevant.

Clustering sanity checks (protocol):
- Human tasks: given a seed item and its top-10 nearest neighbors (model embedding nearest in cosine), label each neighbor: SAME-CLUSTER | RELATED-BUT-NO | DIFFERENT.
- Quick metrics to compute per run:
  * Local Purity@5: fraction of top-5 neighbors labeled SAME-CLUSTER (avg over seeds).
  * Neighbor Entropy: entropy of gold cluster labels in top-10 neighbors.
  * Silhouette snapshot (coarse): for each seed, compute avg intra-cluster similarity vs avg nearest other-cluster similarity; report median.
- Pass/fail heuristics for gating: Local Purity@5 > 0.7 and median silhouette > 0.08 for this spotlight; if both drop by >0.12 relative to baseline, flag for deeper investigation.

Multilingual parity checks (protocol):
- For each translation-equivalent triplet (EN/ES/ZH), compute cosine similarity between language pairs; human double-checks top-3 nearest neighbors for parity.
- Annotation task: given EN query and candidates where one candidate is a translation of the EN gold doc, annotators mark whether candidates are exact translations, semantic-equivalent paraphrases, or divergent content.
- Special handling: code-switched fragments (e.g., "comprar shoes") should be treated as same-language intent; do not penalize for untranslated tokens.

Prompt sets for synthetic query generation (used for augmenting the spotlight):
- Short factoid prompts: "What is X?" "How do I do X?"
- Intent prompts: "Find me [action] for [entity]" e.g., "Find me booking tips for Kyoto in April"
- Paraphrase prompts: 3 diversity templates applying lexical and syntactic changes (templates attached as inline appendix).

Annotation UI suggestions (low effort):
- Single-page HTML with: seed text, language tag, list of neighbors with copyable text, three radio options for each neighbor, short rationale text box (optional), quick keyboard shortcuts (1/2/3), and flag button for weird content (spam/llm hallucination).
- Export: CSV with columns: seed_id, neighbor_rank, neighbor_id, neighbor_text, annotator, label, rationale.

Failure modes to highlight (examples to add to regression tracker):
- Topic drift: high-similarity neighbor that is topically adjacent but fails user intent (e.g., product spec vs how-to).
- Surface-form bias: identical numeric strings or dates cause false positives (e.g., "2021 annual report" vs "2022 annual report").
- Language fallback: model maps non-Latin script queries to Latin-script items incorrectly (e.g., simplified Chinese queries matching transliterated English titles).
- Named-entity conflation: distinct entities with shared tokens ("Apple" the fruit vs "Apple" the company).

Baseline and experiment tracking:
- Each run stores: model id + commit, dataset version (spotlight vX), metric snapshot (Local Purity@5, median silhouette, multilingual parity score, average relevance rating), and top-20 flagged examples for human review.
- Regression triage playbook: if metric delta > threshold, run automated diff on neighbor lists, surface tokens/phrases that changed similarity ranking, and route to model-onboarding owner with triage template.

Small example bundle (6 semantic probes):
- SP-001: Q="refund policy for widget model 2"
  DocA (3): vendor refund policy mentioning "model 2" and steps
  DocB (1): blog discussing popular widgets (mentions model 2 once)
  DocC (0): unrelated product announcement
- SP-002: Q="symptoms of strep throat" (EN) with translations to ES/ZH for multilingual check
- SP-003: Q="¿cómo cancelar suscripción?" (ES) candidate docs include code-switched ticket text -> check parity
- SP-004: Q="best sushi spots near Shibuya" (EN) candidate docs include same cluster long-form travel guide vs Yelp-like short entries
- SP-005: Q="reset password corporate account" edge-case: docs with "reset password" user-facing vs admin instructions (different intent)
- SP-006: Q="化妆教程" (ZH, makeup tutorial) include short video transcript (relevance to visual steps)

How to run (cycle):
- Weekly smoke: run embeddings nearest-neighbor extraction for 500 seeds (subset of spotlight + random product queries), compute metrics, and invite 2 annotators to label top flagged seeds (takes ~2 hrs).
- Release gating: full spotlight run + additional 2x augmentation of paraphrases; require no major regressions vs baseline for release approval.

Appendix: quick annotation heuristics cheat-sheet:
- Prefer usefulness to topical overlap when ranking relevance.
- If a doc contains explicit answer phrases ("You can fix this by..."), favor higher relevance.
- For clusters, prioritize semantic function (instructions vs description) over shared named entities.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Decide final pass/fail numeric thresholds for enterprise customers (tighten silhouette/pass criteria).
- Expand language coverage: add Indonesian and Hindi for next quarter.
- Build small annotation UI template and store on GH for reuse.

Contact / owner: Aisha Kumar (eng-applied-ml). Notes: this is intentionally pragmatic to enable quick cycles; aim for reproducible runs and minimal annotation friction.
